key_insight: WC–Co–Cr coating properties depend on powder morphology and spraying method: detonation spraying favors hardness, while HVOF yields a dense, uniform coating with low friction.
engineering_relevance: Selecting the powder and spraying process can help improve the wear resistance and durability of machine parts operating under high loads and intensive friction.
method: Compare detonation-sprayed and HVOF-deposited WC–Co–Cr coatings.
Examine starting-powder morphology and coating microstructure using SEM and EDS.
Evaluate coating microhardness and tribological behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an average microhardness of 1449 HV for detonation-sprayed coatings and a friction coefficient of Kt = 0.143 for HVOF coatings.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify wear-test conditions, variability, or quantitative wear rates, limiting direct predictions of service performance.
paper_title: INVESTIGATION OF THE FORMATION OF STRUCTURE AND WEAR-RESISTANT PROPERTIES OF WC–CO–CR COATINGS PRODUCED BY HVOF AND DETONATION SPRAYING
